content:
Francis Ngannou is one of the most dominant and fascinating figures in mixed martial arts (MMA) history. Known for his incredible knockout power, physical strength, and inspiring journey from poverty to global stardom, he has left a lasting impact on combat sports. Here’s everything you need to know about him:

---

### **Early Life & Background**
- **Full Name:** Francis Zavier Ngannou
- **Born:** September 5, 1986 (age 37 as of 2024)
- **Birthplace:** Batié, Cameroon
- **Early Struggles:**
  - Grew up in extreme poverty in a small village in Cameroon.
  - Worked in a sand quarry as a child to help his family.
  - Dropped out of school at 10 due to financial hardship.
  - Moved to Paris, France, at 26 (2013) with no money, no MMA experience, and no connections, sleeping on the streets before finding a gym.

---

### **MMA Career**
#### **Early Career (2013–2015)**
- **Amateur Record:** 0-0 (turned pro immediately)
- **Professional Debut:** November 16, 2013 (KO win in France).
- **Early Fights:** Went 5-1 in regional European promotions, showcasing his raw power.

#### **UFC Career (2015–2023)**
- **UFC Debut:** December 19, 2015 (vs. Luis Henrique, TKO win).
- **Rise to Contention:**
  - Won his first 6 UFC fights by knockout (including wins over Andrei Arlovski, Alistair Overeem, and Junior dos Santos).
  - Became known for his **one-punch knockout power**, earning the nickname **"The Predator."**
- **Title Shot & Championship Reign:**
  - **UFC Heavyweight Championship:** Won the title by knocking out Stipe Miocic at **UFC 260 (March 27, 2021)** in a rematch (lost their first fight at UFC 220).
  - **First Defense:** Knocked out Ciryl Gane in **1 minute** at **UFC 270 (January 22, 2022)** to retain the belt.
- **UFC Departure (2023):**
  - Left the UFC in January 2023 after failing to negotiate a new contract. His demands included better pay, healthcare, and fighter sponsorship rights.
  - The UFC stripped him of the title, and he became a free agent.

#### **PFL (2023–Present)**
- **PFL Africa (Super Fight Division):**
  - Signed with the **Professional Fighters League (PFL)** in May 2023, becoming the **PFL Heavyweight Champion** by default (no fights yet).
  - Expected to face **Anthony Joshua** in a **boxing match** (see below).

---

### **Boxing Career**
Ngannou has expressed interest in boxing and has trained with legends like **Mike Tyson** and **Andy Ruiz Jr.**
- **First Boxing Match:** **October 28, 2023** vs. **Tyson Fury** (WBC Heavyweight Champion) in Saudi Arabia.
  - **Result:** **Split Decision Loss** (controversial, many thought Ngannou won).
  - **Performance:** Knocked Fury down in the 3rd round and nearly finished him, proving his boxing potential.
- **Next Fight:** Expected to face **Anthony Joshua** in **2024** (details TBA).

---

### **Fighting Style & Strengths**
- **Striking Power:** One of the hardest punchers in combat sports history.
  - **Punch Force:** Recorded **129,161 units** on a **Punch Force Meter** (highest ever recorded, surpassing Mike Tyson’s 112,000).
  - **Knockout Ratio:** 14 KOs in 20 MMA wins (70% KO rate).
- **Athleticism:** 6'4" with an **83-inch reach**, explosive speed for a heavyweight.
- **Grappling:** Improved over time but remains a **striker-first** fighter.
- **Cardio:** Historically a weakness, but improved in later UFC fights.

---

### **Personal Life & Philanthropy**
- **Family:** Has a daughter (born 2023) with his partner, **Bridgette Motsepe** (sister of South African billionaire Patrice Motsepe).
- **Foundation:** Created the **Francis Ngannou Foundation** to help underprivileged children in Cameroon.
  - Built a **gym in Batié** to train young fighters.
  - Provides **scholarships and food programs** for children.
- **Legal Issues:**
  - Arrested in **2016** in Las Vegas for domestic violence (charges later dropped).
  - Denied entry to the **UK in 2018** due to his criminal record.

---

### **Net Worth & Business Ventures**
- **Estimated Net Worth (2024):** **$10–15 million** (from UFC, PFL, boxing, and endorsements).
- **Endorsements:**
  - **Under Armour** (signature shoes)
  - **Monster Energy**
  - **Venom** (MMA gear)
  - **Crypto.com**
- **Media Appearances:**
  - Featured in **ESPN’s "30 for 30"** documentary (*"Francis Ngannou: The Baddest Man on the Planet"*).
  - Appeared in **WWE** (2022) and **Fast & Furious** (cameo in *Fast X*, 2023).

---

### **Legacy & Impact**
- **First African UFC Heavyweight Champion** (a major milestone for MMA in Africa).
- **Inspiration for African Fighters:** Proved that fighters from impoverished backgrounds can reach the top.
- **Cross-Sport Star:** One of the few MMA fighters to compete at a high level in **boxing** against elite heavyweights.
- **Fighter Advocacy:** Pushed for **better pay and healthcare** for UFC fighters, influencing contract negotiations.

---

### **Controversies & Feuds**
- **UFC Contract Dispute:** Left the UFC over **pay and fighter rights**, calling out Dana White for "exploiting fighters."
- **Dana White Feud:** White called Ngannou **"ungrateful"** after his departure.
- **Ciryl Gane Rivalry:** Had a heated feud with Gane before their UFC 270 fight (Ngannou won by decision).
- **Jon Jones:** Ngannou has criticized Jones for avoiding him in the UFC.

---

### **Future Plans**
- **Boxing:** Likely to face **Anthony Joshua** in 2024 (potentially for a **WBA/WBC interim title**).
- **MMA:** Could return to MMA if a big-money fight (e.g., vs. **Jon Jones** or **Stipe Miocic**) materializes.
- **Acting:** Expanding into Hollywood (already in *Fast X*).

---

### **Fun Facts**
- **Nicknames:** "The Predator," "The Cameroon Colossus," "The Baddest Man on the Planet."
- **Languages:** Speaks **French, English, and several Cameroonian dialects**.
- **Hobbies:** Loves **soccer** (supports **Paris Saint-Germain**) and **photography**.
- **Idols:** **Mike Tyson** (boxing) and **Fedor Emelianenko** (MMA).

---

### **Record & Achievements**
| **Category**       | **Details** |
|--------------------|------------|
| **MMA Record**     | 17-3 (14 KOs, 0 Subs) |
| **UFC Record**     | 12-3 (UFC Heavyweight Champion) |
| **PFL Record**     | 0-0 (PFL Heavyweight Champion) |
| **Boxing Record**  | 0-1 (vs. Tyson Fury) |
| **Knockout of the Year** | vs. Alistair Overeem (UFC Fight Night 134, 2018) |
| **Fight of the Year** | vs. Stipe Miocic (UFC 260, 2021) |
| **ESPY Award**     | 2021 (Best MMA Fighter) |

---

### **Conclusion**
Francis Ngannou is more than just a fighter—he’s a **global icon** who overcame unimaginable hardship to become a champion. His **knockout power, charisma, and philanthropy** have made him one of the most beloved figures in combat sports. Whether in **MMA, boxing, or entertainment**, he continues to break barriers and inspire millions.
